Verified against the file at `artifacts/editorial/release-candidates/transit/coquitlam-como-lake-bc-hydro-work.mdx` — local `sha256sum` matches the requested digest exactly, so this is the exact release candidate.

## Factual support and source use — clean

I fetched the cited primary source live (City of Coquitlam notice #2008) rather than relying on the pipeline's evidence record. Every load-bearing claim checks out verbatim:

| Claim in candidate | Source |

| Como Lake Ave, Clarke Rd → North Rd | "Como Lake Avenue between Clarke Road and North Road" |
| Starts Wed July 29, ends Fri Aug. 7 | matches |
| 9 a.m.–3 p.m. | matches |
| No listed work Sun Aug. 2, Mon Aug. 3 | "Excluded Dates: Sunday, August 2 and Monday, August 3" |

Note: the contact details are **not** in the pipeline's `primaryFacts` list in `2026-07-27-1230-researched-candidates.json`, so I checked them independently against the page — they are correct. Same for the alternate-route advice, which I re-fetched with a targeted prompt to confirm it is real source wording and not an inference.

**Calendar arithmetic independently confirmed:** 2026-07-29 = Wednesday, 2026-08-07 = Friday, 2026-08-02 = Sunday, 2026-08-03 = Monday. All four day-name claims are correct.

**Source URL is correct as cited.** The `/m/` path looks like a mobile variant, so I tested the non-`/m/` form — `https://www.coquitlam.ca/newsflash/Home/Detail/2008` returns **404**. The cited URL is the working one; do not "clean it up."

## Unsupported claims — none

The two negative claims are properly hedged and accurate: "not listed as a full road closure" and "The version checked by Trends Today does not list a separate overnight work window or a city detour map" (source lists daytime hours only, no detour map). The one inference — "If your trip can move outside the listed hours, that may be the easiest way to avoid the construction delay" — is hedged and follows directly from the stated hours.

## Integrity checks

- **Image**: file exists at declared path; valid PNG, 1672×941, which is the house standard shared by 11 of 14 sampled editorial images.
- **AI disclosure is actually visible to readers** — I confirmed `imageAttribution` renders as an on-image caption at `apps/web/app/posts/[slug]/page.tsx:122-126`, not as hidden metadata. Alt text hedges correctly ("Coquitlam-**style** road"), making no claim to be the real work zone.
- **Frontmatter**: parses cleanly; `readingTime: 2` matches 321 words; title 47 chars, description 130, subtitle 121 — all in range and accurate. `editor: "Moe"` is an established convention (25 files use it).
- **Not a duplicate**: the three sibling Coquitlam transit pieces cover different locations/dates; the only other "Como Lake" mention is in the road-safety-plan article about intersection upgrades — unrelated.
- **Single primary source** matches the bar used by comparable published bulletins (Burrard elevator, Surrey stewardship).
- **Legal/reputational**: low-risk civic bulletin, no named individuals, no allegations, contact line is the city's public number.

## Non-blocking polish notes

1. **Hero image is off-season.** It shows leafless deciduous trees, grey overcast sky, wet pavement — reads as winter/early spring, not late July in Metro Vancouver. It asserts nothing false and is labeled AI-generated, so this doesn't block, but a summer-looking replacement would serve readers better.
2. **Over-sectioned for 321 words.** Five H2s, and "Where to ask questions" is a single sentence under its own heading. Consider folding it into the planning section.
3. **Filler line.** "For planning, the useful details are the named segment, the midday work hours, and the listed lane reduction" restates what the reader just read; "The version checked by Trends Today does not list…" is somewhat meta.
4. **Zero internal links** despite three closely related Coquitlam transit pieces. `CLAUDE.md:287` says "Internal link when relevant" (soft), and 41 of 161 published articles have none — so this is guidance, not a gate.
5. **Title compresses the range.** "July 29 to Aug. 7" omits the two-day gap, which the body corrects. Standard headline practice; the city frames it the same way.

Nothing in the candidate is inaccurate, unsupported, mislabeled, or legally risky. Clear to publish as-is; items 1–4 are optional improvements.
